stem.text: People enter a park at a rate of E(t) people per hour, where E is differentiable and t is measured in hours after the park opens. Measured values are E(0) = 30, E(1) = 50, E(3) = 60, E(4) = 40. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{4} E(t)\,dt \), the number of people who enter the park from t = 0 to t = 4, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 1 \cdot \frac{30 + 50}{2} = 40 \); \( 2 \cdot \frac{50 + 60}{2} = 110 \); \( 1 \cdot \frac{60 + 40}{2} = 50 \).

distractor_derivations.A: trapezoidal sum with the common width (b - a)/3 used for every subinterval
distractor_derivations.B: trapezoid area taken as width times the sum of the two endpoint values, with no division by 2
distractor_derivations.D: factor 1/2 applied to the last trapezoid only
